
*Design Ground Motions* for critical infrastructure will have a target Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) defined according to the failure consequences rating for a given target service level (construction, operation, closure, or post-closure). Design ground motions can be selected using either a consequence-based (deterministic) or a risk-based (probabilistic) approach. The probabilistic approach evaluates the seismic demand of a wide range of seismic ground motions on the facilities to satisfy a tolerable risk criterion based on failure probabilities. In contrast, the deterministic approach requires the selection of design earthquakes considering the failure consequences of the facility. Under this approach, the target Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) for critical infrastructure is defined according to the failure consequence rating for a given target service level (construction, operation, closure, or post-closure).

The consequence-based seismic design of a critical facility must ensure a very low probability of failure for a maximum design earthquake and an acceptable level of damage for an earthquake likely to occur during the facility’s service life. The facility’s service life encompass all phases of construction and operation, periods of temporary cessation of operations, and the closure phase (transition phase into post-closure, also referred to as active-care closure). Post-closure refers to permanently closed facilities configured for their perpetual form/state, subjected to the maximum time of exposure irrespective of the facility’s consequence classification.

Many agencies, such as CDA [-@CDA14], ANCOLD [-@ANCOLD12], and GISTM [-@gistm2020], have **dual performance criteria** to address the safety and serviceability of Tailings Storage Facilities. Safety considerations primarily focus on the ultimate limit state, utilizing an upper-level earthquake known as the maximum design earthquake (MDE) or Safety Evaluation Earthquake (SEE). Serviceability analysis ensures that the TSF remains operational after minor seismic events and that any damage is manageable and repairable. For this service level, a lower-level earthquake known as the Operating Basis Earthquake (OBE) is assumed. This dual consideration helps in maintaining the functionality of TSFs and mitigating risks associated with operational interruptions or failures. In regions of moderate-to high seismicity, it is necessary to explicitly consider serviceability conditions, as residual displacements can be significant and affect the operation of the structure.


> The Tailings Storage Facilities at `r params$project` site has been classified with grade **`r params$risk_rating`**, according to GISTM [-@gistm2020], adopting a target AEP of `r params$mde` as the maximum design earthquake **MDE** ^[In regions of low seismicity, compliance with safety considerations (limit states) is generally sufficient to ensure serviceability conditions, due to the magnitude of the residual displacements associated with the maximum design earthquakes.]. For all facilities, the maximum design earthquake (MDE) has been adopted to address both safety and serviceability criteria across all project stages, including post-closure stages.
